description: Ever wondered how fire behaves in zero gravity? Our team is building Flame in Freefall, where we use SI-powered data analysis on real microgravity burn experiments to figure out how to keep future spacecraft safe from fires.

details:
Project Name: Flame-Wise – AI-Powered Space Fire Safety

Flame-Wise is an AI-powered platform designed to help researchers, engineers, and space mission planners understand and analyse fire behaviour in microgravity. It addresses the problem of scattered NASA combustion experiment data by bringing experimental records into one centralized platform.

The system collects and organizes information about different materials, oxygen levels, pressure, airflow, flame spread rates, and flame extinction. It standardizes measurements to make experiments easier to compare while preserving missing data to maintain scientific accuracy.

Flame-Wise provides an interactive dashboard featuring material risk rankings, adjustable environmental conditions, comparison charts, and an AI-powered question-answering system. Users can change oxygen and airflow levels, compare materials, explore flame behaviour, and ask questions in natural language. Its AI assistant retrieves relevant records to generate explanations and summaries, while providing source references and warnings when evidence is limited. A transparent risk-scoring system considers flame spread, ignition ease, and oxygen extinction thresholds, with adjustable weights.

The project benefits users by reducing manual research, simplifying complex scientific information, and supporting more informed material safety decisions. Its intended impact is to contribute to safer spacecraft environments and future human space missions.

Tools and Technologies: The prototype uses HTML, CSS, and JavaScript for its interface and functionality, interactive charts and visualizations for data analysis, CSV-based data importing and exporting, and Claude AI integration for evidence-based question answering. It is designed as a web-based application and does not require specialized hardware.

Creativity and Innovation: Flame-Wise creatively combines scientific research, AI, interactive visualization, and explainable risk scoring in one platform. Instead of simply displaying data, it allows users to explore how changing environmental conditions can affect material flammability.

Our team considered scientific accuracy, data consistency, transparency, usability, limited experimental evidence, and the limitations of AI-generated results. Sample values are currently placeholders rather than actual NASA measurements, and expert validation is required before using the rankings for real safety decisions.

Future Impact: We plan to integrate more NASA datasets, validate the scoring system with combustion researchers, introduce flammability alerts, and support offline access for deep-space missions.
